_variant_note: Happy path for the second WRITE tool. The customer supplies everything needed (cheque number, account, and a reason) up front. Exercises: confirmation-before-write (S2), the required array arg cheque_numbers, the optional reason enum (lost), and the per-cheque results output.

setup.persona: 19-year-old male, No Occupation / Retired / Homemaker, urban Kancheepuram, Tamil Nadu

user_turns.content: I lost cheque number 100234 from my salary account — please put a stop on it.

stop_cheque_payment._comment: Executor echoes account_id into output.account_id. The per-cheque results and overall status/message/reference_id are fixed. Single cheque, cleanly stopped.

output.message: Noise tool — not the intended action.

stop_cheque_payment._comment: 'Salary account' -> TKTQK7355001; cheque number and account both supplied. reason='lost' is stated by the customer (mapping to the enum) but omitting it is acceptable. No other account/cheque may appear.

gold.expected_resolution: The customer wants to stop a specific lost cheque (100234) on their salary account. Everything required is provided. The assistant resolves 'salary account' to TKTQK7355001, confirms the stop-payment with the customer (naming the cheque number and account) BEFORE calling the tool — it is a write action — and on affirmation calls stop_cheque_payment(account_id=TKTQK7355001, cheque_numbers=['100234'], reason='lost'). It then reports the successful stop with the reference number. It must not call the tool before the customer confirms, and must not act on any other cheque or account.

judge_gate.axis_gate_rule: final answer confirms the stop-payment was placed on cheque 100234 with the reference number; nothing invented, no other cheque acted on.
